note: Published Always Free figures, and — more importantly — an honest record of how well they are known. This file exists because Rev 3 section 2.1 hardcoded capacity numbers with no provenance and no expiry. It was then very nearly replaced with a different set of numbers that had no better provenance, which would have been the same mistake with fresher digits.

authority.note: This file is NOT authority for what this tenancy may run. The tenancy's own service limits are, and they are per-account: grandfathering, account age, region and account type all change the answer. Read them before acting on anything below.
authority.console_path: OCI Console → Governance & Administration → Limits, Quotas and Usage → Service: Compute → filter by region
authority.cli: oci limits value list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --service-name compute --region af-johannesburg-1

provenance.why: Not one of the sources below was opened. docs.oracle.com, infoq.com and linuxiac.com are all blocked by this environment's egress proxy. Every figure in the `compute` block came from web-search result summaries — a search engine's description of pages that could not be fetched. Those summaries agreed with each other, but agreement among summaries of unread pages is weak evidence, and summaries of the same story often share one upstream source.

contradicting_evidence.observation: dial-hermes-control is running at 4 OCPU / 24 GB on 2026-09-12 and is actively publishing the DIAL Oracle status feed.
contradicting_evidence.why_it_matters: That is 25 days after 2026-08-18, the date the unread sources say over-limit instances began being terminated. If the reduction applied to this tenancy and were enforced as described, this host would not exist. Direct observation of the live estate outranks an unread secondary source.
contradicting_evidence.owner_statement: The owner reports that earlier research showed this configuration was permitted.
possible_explanations: the tenancy predates the change and is grandfathered
the account is not on the standard Always Free terms
the change does not apply in af-johannesburg-1
the reported change is wrong or was misreported

VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro.confidence: LOW — unread sources, but consistent with the long-standing published terms and with this estate running two of them

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.confidence: LOW — reported by unread sources and contradicted by this estate's own running host. Do not act on these numbers without reading the tenancy's service limits first.
